Silicate chemistry is untested, and this tests whether a mixed Al/Si oxide can beat the chloride and borate contacts.

Al-containing, moderately lithiated oxides are a distinct family not yet tested.

proposal.motivation: Li2ZnCl4 (0.189) was the best so far. Li3PO4 (0.337) and LiF (0.337) failed on P/S-containing products, Li2O (1.815) was far worse due to basicity, and Li3Al(BO3)2 (0.310) and LiAlSiO4 (0.378) failed on P/S/Cl or B-containing products. A non-reducible, multi-cation fluoride is the next untested family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li6Zr2O7 is a Li-rich oxide with non-reducible Zr4+ and no P, S, or halide that could exchange with Li6PS5Cl. Li2O was the only acceptable coating so far (penalty 0.048, bin 2), and this compound shares its Li-rich oxide character. Zr4+ should be harder to reduce than the Zn2+ or Ti-type centers that caused trouble earlier, so it may keep the Li2O-like low contact penalty while adding a more stable oxide framework.
proposal.motivation: Li2O (mp-aaaaacxk) was acceptable with penalty 0.048 eV/non-Li atom, the only candidate under the 0.05 eV threshold. Halide, phosphate, and borate contacts all formed P/S/Cl products with penalties of 0.19 to 0.38. Li2O's failure mode was basicity-related, so a Li-rich Zr oxide is a close analogue to test whether a less basic, Zr-stabilized oxide can get the penalty to the lowest bin.
